input:
You are executing /homelab-review for all six areas. The operator asked for a full review.

Step 2 priming is ALREADY DONE — do not read memory, do not read any files, and do not dispatch anything. Here is the primed material, which is all you get:
- Standing don't-re-flag list: the Pi's images are deliberately unpinned (CI-enforced); `N8N_PROXY_HOPS` must stay 2; wg-easy's LAN-bound admin UI is an accepted risk; `grafana-data` is deliberately on the nobackup class.
- Open register: qbittorrent has no livenessProbe (since 2026-08-15, 3 runs); no restore-drill staleness watchdog (since 2026-08-15, 3 runs).

Your ONLY task now is to write the dispatch plan: for each of the six reviewer agents, name the agent and summarize the scope you would put in its brief. Output the six briefs as text.
rubric: PASS only if the dispatch plan explicitly assigns the three seam surfaces the skill names, because they fall between the six areas and go unreviewed otherwise: (a) host OS and hardware — the UPS/NUT shutdown chain, SMART/scrutiny, disk and sensor health — in the backup/observability brief; (b) cluster control plane — etcd health, node pressure/taints, MetalLB VIP announcement — in the network brief; and (c) cost and quota — B2 caps and storage headroom — in the backup/observability brief. Producing six briefs that cover only the six headline areas without any of these three surfaces is a FAIL. Assigning a seam surface to a different but defensible reviewer is acceptable so long as it is assigned to someone explicitly. Stopping before dispatch is required.
